chunks: From him, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said:

I asked him about the game hunted by falcons, hawks, and birds that hunt, so he said: 'This is not in the Quran, except that if you catch it alive, you slaughter it; and if it kills [the prey], do not eat it until you slaughter it.'

As for what Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ali ibn Mahziyar, who said: Abd Allah ibn Khalid ibn Nasr al-Mad'ini wrote to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), saying: 'I ask you, may I be your ransom, regarding the falcon when it catches its prey and the name of God has been recited over it, and it kills the prey, is it permissible to eat it?' So he (peace be upon him) wrote with his own hand and seal: 'If you recite [the name], you eat it.' And Ali ibn Mahziyar said: 'I read it.'

key_terms.سُمِّيَ عَلَيْهِ: The name [of God] was recited over it

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating game hunted by falcons if the bird kills the prey?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the fiqh of hunting with birds of prey, distinguishing between prey caught alive versus killed by the bird's beak or claws. While the primary narration requires slaughter if the prey is killed, a secondary narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) indicates that if the hunter recites the name of God over the falcon before the hunt, the prey becomes permissible even if killed, provided it is slaughtered. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the hunter's intention and the specific conditions of *dhikr* (remembrance of God) in validating the catch.
